report:
log.mining.query.filter.mode not working

Hi,We have a huge Oracle Database where we do CDC from. We capture about 50 tables with "table.include.list". There are many hundreds of tables that we are not interested in. Everything generally works well with a few seconds of lag, but from time to time, some irrelevant table is flooded with records and then we can see that we get really high lag on the connector. To optimize for that, we added the
"log.mining.query.filter.mode: in" which says to perform "...extremely well if you have a lot of schema or table include/exclude list options defined in your configuration. And finally, because this choice performs database-level filtering, this reduces the network latency and only returns the necessary rows to the connector.".  Perfect!
It also says:
"This mode is often useful when capturing a large number of tables from a database that is heavily saturated with changes. The generated query is much more complex than the none mode, and focuses on reducing network overhead and performing as much filtering at the database level as possible.
Finally, do not specify regular expressions as part of schema and table include/exclude configuration properties. Using regular expressions will cause the connector to not match changes based on these configuration properties, causing changes to be missed.
But when we apply that option, the connector stops capturing data. We get no error messages. The connector apparently gets it, because when we remove that option everything works well again. What are we doing wrong? Are we using regexp without knowing it?
Config:
config:
    ...
    log.mining.strategy: online_catalog
    log.mining.query.filter.mode: in
    table.include.list: |-
        db.table1,
        db.table2,
        ...
        db.table50
    message.key.columns: |-
        db.table1:prop1,prop2;
        db.table2:prop1,prop2,prop3;
        ...
        db.table50:prop1;

evidence.quote: We recently found an issue where configuration parsing was not trimming whitespaces between comma-separated elements... This should be fixed in Debezium 2.5.1.Final and 2.6.0.Alpha1

notes: With log.mining.query.filter.mode=in and a multi-line table.include.list, untrimmed whitespace ended up in the IN-clause table names so nothing matched; reporter suspected their own regex misuse. Config list parsing / IN-clause builder code settles it.
